identification.name: UHMW-PE (Ultra High Molecular Weight Polyethylene)
identification.common_form_notes: Widely available as compression-moulded or ram-extruded sheet, plate, round bar, and tube from plastics distributors. Machines well with sharp tooling and adequate chip clearance; very high melt viscosity makes it unsuitable for conventional injection moulding or 3D printing.
identification.notes: Semi-crystalline thermoplastic with molecular weight ≥4.2 million g/mol (vs. ~0.5 million for standard HDPE), giving exceptional abrasion resistance, a very low coefficient of friction, high impact toughness (retained even at low temperature), and good chemical/corrosion resistance. Self-lubricating — commonly run dry against itself or steel. Data below are Garland Manufacturing's GAR-DUR® grade as reported by MatWeb, representative of generic unfilled, non-cross-linked virgin UHMW-PE. No tensile (Young's) modulus was reported by the source; the 1210 MPa flexural modulus (1% secant, ASTM D790B) is used in its place. Poisson's ratio (0.46) is a typical literature value for HDPE/UHMW-PE (Callister), not from the MatWeb source. usable_temp_range is derived from data in the source: −40 °C from Izod unnotched impact testing showing no break (NB) at −40 °C (ASTM D256A); 80 °C from heat deflection temperature at the lower 0.46 MPa (66 psi) load (ASTM D648) — HDT drops to 47 °C at the higher 1.8 MPa (264 psi) load, so stiffness under sustained higher stress falls off well below 80 °C. Coefficient of friction: 0.11 (UHMW-PE to UHMW-PE), 0.13 (to stainless steel), 0.14 (to rolled steel). Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 44.1/1.732 ≈ 25.5 MPa. Melting point reported as a narrow crystalline range (130–131 °C); the lower bound is stored. Glass transition temperature was not reported by the source and is left null rather than mixing in an unsourced literature value.

typical_usage: Wear strips, liners, and guides for chutes, hoppers, and conveyors in mining, pulp and paper, and bulk material handling; sprockets, gears, and bushings requiring a low coefficient of friction and self-lubricating dry-running performance; food-processing and refrigeration equipment; impact-resistant guards and wear plates replacing steel in abrasive or corrosive service.
